text:
The period from 2 to 21 was defined by expansion, internal decay, and fragmentation. The Wougate Crown began by seizing empty land and defeating its rival, the Reswoumark Crown, but ended divided after a succession dispute. Five people held the seat, with an average tenure of 3.8 years. The power fought two battles, both won, and spent two years at war. It sent two raids that carried off plunder and suffered seven raids, all beaten off. Hunger and sickness lasted ten years, killing 450 people and driving 471 from their homes.

The Wougate Crown occupied Thu Pits in 2 and declared war on the Reswoumark Crown in 5 for Wei Seam. Its allies defeated the Reswoumark Crown at Wei Seam in 5, killing 29, and took the site. In 6, it defeated the Reswoumark Crown at Reswoumark, killing 198, and took that settlement. The Reswoumark Crown was finished in 6, its last 4 followers scattering. Peace was made in 7. The Wougate Crown married into House Wem in 3 and 5. Famine struck Thu Pits in 5, killing 22. House Wem raided Wougate in 10, carrying off 51 grain and killing 52, and raided Haelabarrow in 11, carrying off 32 grain and killing 50.

Sus Waernthaeld died in 12. Famine in Wougate killed 181 that year. Thris Pou took the seat in 12 by right of birth. Haelabarrow rose against the Wougate Crown in 12, whose standing had fallen very low. Krim Groum challenged Thris Pou openly in 13, won, and took the seat. Thris Pou was cast out. The Wougate Crown raided Broldtemoor in 13, carrying off 45 grain and killing 56. Deathder Grun challenged Krim Groum openly in 14, won, and took the seat. Krim Groum was cast out. The Wougate Crown raided Rucrag in 15, carrying off 29 grain and killing 35.

Naenddaem Houllteind returned from exile in 16. His conspiracy against Deathder Grun was uncovered in 20 after 1 years. Naenddaem Houllteind was cast out in 20. Thrir Pondsurn had Deathder Grun murdered in 21. Deathder Grun was killed by Thrir Pondsurn at Reswoumark. Lea Dae contested the claim of Skobas Frul in 21. Lea Dae took the seat, setting aside Skobas Frul. The Wougate Crown was divided: Skobas Frul carried off 2 places as the Second Crown of Reswoumark. Wei Seam rose against the Wougate Crown in 19, whose standing had fallen to nothing.

The period from 42 to 50 was defined by the collapse of the Wougate Crown’s territorial integrity and its subsequent struggle for survival through dynastic alliances. At the start, the Crown faced a war declared by House Wem over a long-standing grievance, a conflict that resulted in the loss of its capital, Wougate, and the defeat of its forces. The Crown’s standing deteriorated rapidly, losing its seat and its primary settlement within the first two years. By the end of the period, the Crown had regained neither its lost territory nor its former military strength, relying instead on a series of marriages to bind itself to House Wem and the Sworn Men of Rucrag.

The initial phase of the period saw the Wougate Crown defeated twice by House Wem at Wougate, with 180 dead in 42 and 150 dead in 43. House Wem took Wougate from the Crown in 43, and the two powers made peace after two years of war following the collapse of the Crown’s position. During this time, internal instability weakened the Crown further. Voun Woldlom, who had held the seat since 38, was cast out in 43 for an attempted murder on Lea Dae. Drithne Draend took the seat in 43 by right of birth but was also cast out in 46 after an attempt on Kurnsa Bealldo failed. Halweill Tu took the seat in 46 by right of birth and remained holding it at the end of the period.

The Crown’s military efforts during the remainder of the period were uniformly unsuccessful. It sent three raids, all of which were beaten off: against Thu Pits in 45, Wei Seam in 49, and Wougate in 50. It suffered one raid in 42 by the Sworn Men of Rucrag at Wougate, which carried off 53 grain and killed 27. To secure its position, the Crown entered three marriages. Drithne Draend married Feald Keim in 46, binding the Crown to House Wem. Halweill Tu married Threihoull Thild in 48, binding the Crown to the Sworn Men of Rucrag. Steaskaes Ve married Bi Binseall in 50, further binding the Crown to the Sworn Men of Rucrag. The quarrel between the Wougate Crown and House Wem persisted, marked by two battles between them.

The Reswoumark Crown’s rule ended in the span of three years, collapsing under the weight of external conquest and internal betrayal. At the start of the period, the power held Wei Seam and Reswoumark, but its authority was already fracturing. A famine at Wei Seam in year 4 killed six people and left grain short by 2. The crisis deepened in year 5, when 13 more died and 31 abandoned the place. These losses provided the pretext for the Wougate Crown to declare war on the Reswoumark Crown for control of Wei Seam.

The Wougate Crown and its allies defeated the Reswoumark Crown at Wei Seam, killing 29 people, and took the site. The conflict moved to Reswoumark in year 6, where the Wougate Crown and its allies defeated the Reswoumark Crown again, killing 198 people and taking the settlement. Within the Reswoumark leadership, Fornhir Threi had Diska Louth murdered at Reswoumark. Diska Louth, ruler of the Reswoumark Crown, was killed by Fornhir Threi at Reswoumark. The Reswoumark Crown was finished, landless, with its last 4 followers scattering.

The period ended in year 7 with the Wougate Crown and the Reswoumark Crown making peace after 2 years, following the collapse of the Reswoumark Crown. The power that began the period holding territory was destroyed within it, its end marked by the scattering of its final followers.

The period from 22 to 41 was defined by a war with House Wem that lasted four years and ended in exhaustion, followed by a succession of rulers who held the seat for an average of 2.7 years each. The Wougate Crown began the period with Lea Dae in the seat, but the war and internal instability quickly reshaped the power. Seven people held the seat during these twenty years; four were cast out, two were killed, and one remained holding it at the end. The conflict with House Wem resulted in two victories and two defeats for the Wougate Crown, with the loss of Thu Pits and Wei Seam.

In 22, House Wem declared war on the Wougate Crown and broke its alliance. Thrir Pondsurn challenged Lea Dae for the Wougate Crown and won, taking the seat by coup and casting Lea Dae out. The Wougate Crown defeated House Wem at Thu Pits, killing 24, and again at Thu Pits in 23, killing 20. However, Thrir Pondsurn was cast out in 23 after an attempt on Tin Kaes failed. Tommarn Ri took the seat by setting aside the claim of the named heir Haepin Maerba, but was cast out in 24 after a failed attempt on Tin Kaes. House Wem and its allies defeated the Wougate Crown at Thu Pits, killing 16, and took Thu Pits. Sillmaem Freith took the seat by right of birth.

Sillmaem Freith ordered the murders of Tin Kaes, Goul Geall, and Rein Ga at Broldtemoor in 25, 26, and 27 respectively. In 26, House Wem and the Wougate Crown made peace after four years of war. Kros Ranu’s conspiracy against Sillmaem Freith was uncovered, and Kros Ranu was executed. In 28, Pondfern Lull married Koldfaem Trir, binding the Wougate Crown to House Wem. A plague broke out at Wougate in 28, killing 95, and in 29, killing 195 more and causing 187 to flee. The Wougate Crown’s raids on Thu Pits, Wei Seam, and Broldtemoor were all beaten off.

Kurnsa Bealldo murdered Sillmaem Freith at Wougate in 31. Neildpoun Porn took the seat by right of birth. In 32, Voun Woldlom married Mith Thres, binding the Wougate Crown to the Second Crown of Reswoumark. Kurnsa Bealldo’s conspiracy against Neildpoun Porn was uncovered in 34, and Kurnsa Bealldo was cast out. Thraellgul Thalgin challenged Neildpoun Porn openly in 35, won, and took the seat, killing Neildpoun Porn. Thraellgul Thalgin married Naerream Thrurei in 36, binding the Wougate Crown to House Wem.

Thraellgul Thalgin was cast out in 38 after an attempt on Koldfaem Trir failed. House Wem raided Wougate, carrying off 33 grain and killing 28. Voun Woldlom took the seat by right of birth. The period ended in 41 with Voun Woldlom still holding the seat. The Wougate Crown and House Wem fought four battles between them. Three people were courted away from the ruler. The Wougate Crown suffered one raid, which carried off plunder.

House Wem spent the twenty years from 29 to 48 as a power defined by internal violence and external raids, ending with its ruler Kurnsa Bealldo still holding the seat. The period began with the Wougate Crown’s raid on Thu Pits beaten off, and concluded with House Wem defeating the Sworn Men of Rucrag at Rucrag. Throughout the era, the house suffered eleven raids, all of which were beaten off, while sending out four raids that carried off plunder or took nothing. Its standing fluctuated, falling very low in 34 when Thu Pits rose against it, before recovering enough to take Wougate from the Wougate Crown in 43.

The seat passed through five rulers, four of whom were killed. Sir Tintoull took the seat in 30 by challenging Kraeth Weageir openly and killing him at Broldtemoor. Koldfaem Trir had Sir Tintoull murdered in 35 and took the seat by election. Lea Dae returned from exile in 38, took the seat by election in 39 after Koldfaem Trir was killed by Greandoul Krean, and was himself murdered by Kurnsa Bealldo in 44. Kurnsa Bealldo took the seat by election later that year and remained there at the end of the period. Naerream Thrurei challenged Kurnsa Bealldo in 45, lost, and was killed by him.

House Wem engaged in two wars, spending two years at war. It declared war on the Wougate Crown in 42 over a long-standing grievance, breaking its alliance with them. It defeated the Wougate Crown at Wougate in 42 with 180 dead and again in 43 with 150 dead, taking Wougate from them. Peace was made in 44 after the collapse of the Wougate Crown. In 48, House Wem declared war on the Sworn Men of Rucrag, breaking its alliance with them, and defeated them at Rucrag with 178 dead. The quarrel between House Wem and the Wougate Crown persisted, resulting in two battles between them.

House Wem’s twenty-year span from 9 to 28 was defined by internal bloodshed and a volatile war with the Wougate Crown. The period began with the house purging its own, as Naenddaem Houllteind was cast out and declared an outlaw for attempting to murder Bae Raer. This internal violence continued as Wealdaern Leasha had Bae Raer killed, and Thrirnum Skou had Pampei Robum killed, leaving five rulers dead by violence and one cast out before the period closed. The house’s standing eroded from these purges, leading to the loss of Rucrag to the Sworn Men of Rucrag in 22 and Wei Seam’s rebellion in 27, when its standing had fallen to nothing.

The conflict with the Wougate Crown dominated the latter half of the period. House Wem declared war in 22, breaking its alliance with the crown. The war saw four battles: House Wem lost to the Wougate Crown at Thu Pits in 22 and 24, but won at Thu Pits in 24 and Wei Seam in 25. These victories allowed House Wem to take Thu Pits and Wei Seam from the Wougate Crown. The war ended in 26 with both sides exhausted. During this time, House Wem sent seven raids, two of which carried off plunder, while five were beaten off. It suffered two raids from the Wougate Crown, both of which carried off plunder.

Succession within House Wem was unstable, passing through seven people with an average rule of 2.7 years. Pampei Robum took the seat by election in 15, followed by Wealdaern Leasha in 16. Tin Kaes won an open challenge in 23, and Goul Geall took the seat by setting aside the named heir Lo Leand in 25. Rein Ga took the seat by election in 26, and Kraeth Weageir took it in 27 by setting aside the named heir Greandoul Krean. Kraeth Weageir held the seat at the end of the period. Marriages tied the house to the Wougate Crown in 24 and 25, and to the Sworn Men of Rucrag in 24.

The Sworn Men of Rucrag spent twenty-nine years defined by a cycle of broken alliances and violent succession. The period began with Rucrag breaking from House Wem in 22, placing Difearn Kaerheald in the seat. The new power quickly stabilized through the return of exiles, including Naenddaem Houllteind, Lea Dae, and Thrir Pondsurn, while Lea Dae’s marriage to Goul Geall bound the Sworn Men to House Wem. This stability ended in 30 when Tommarn Ri challenged and defeated Difearn Kaerheald, taking the seat. Tommarn’s rule was short-lived; he was murdered by Lea Dae in 35. Lea Dae then contested the claim of the named heir, Naenddaem Houllteind, but lost the election. Lea Dae was cast out, and Naenddaem took the seat.

Naenddaem’s tenure was brief and marked by internal violence. He attempted to murder Koldfaem Trir in 36 and was cast out for the attempt. Greandoul Krean took the seat by election. His rule saw a plague at Rucrag in 37 that killed 121 people, and he ordered the murder of Koldfaem Trir at Broldtemoor in 39. Greandoul’s own rule ended in 48 when he attempted to murder Kurnsa Bealldo and was cast out. Threihoull Thild took the seat by election. Threihoull was killed by Kurnsa Bealldo in 49, and Skove Pull took the seat by election. Skove Pull was killed by Kurnsa Bealldo in 50, and Bi Binseall took the seat by election, still holding it at the end of the period.

The power’s external relations were dominated by a quarrel with House Wem that resulted in two battles, both lost. The Sworn Men sent five raids: one against Wougate carried off plunder, while raids on Thu Pits, Wei Seam, Haelabarrow, and Broldtemoor were beaten off. They suffered one raid on Rucrag by House Wem in 47, which took nothing. The period ended with peace between House Wem and the Sworn Men after two years of war, leaving Bi Binseall in the seat.

The Second Crown of Reswoumark spent thirty-one years defined by internal instability and external vulnerability. It began in 21 when Skobas Frul separated from the Wougate Crown to establish the new power. The early years were marked by demographic collapse, as a plague at Haelabarrow killed 304 people in 24 and another 96 in 25, with 200 more fleeing. Despite this, Skobas Frul held the seat until his death in 30. He was succeeded by Mith Thres, who ruled for ten years before attempting to murder Lea Dae in 40. Mith Thres was cast out for that attempt, and the seat passed to Difearn Kaerheald, the named heir, whose claim was upheld against Kurnsa Bealldo.

Difearn Kaerheald’s rule was brief and violent. He held the seat for only two years before being killed by Kurnsa Bealldo in 42. His death triggered a collapse in authority, allowing Haelabarrow to rise against the Second Crown of Reswoumark, whose standing had fallen to nothing. Thraellgul Thalgin took the seat by right of birth in 42, but his tenure was also short-lived. He attempted to murder Kurnsa Bealldo in 47 and was cast out. Voun Woldlom succeeded him by right of birth, ruling for four years before attempting to murder Kurnsa Bealldo in 51 and being cast out.

The period ended with Greandoul Krean taking the seat by right of birth in 51. The Second Crown of Reswoumark had fought one battle, which it lost to House Wem at Haelabarrow in 51, resulting in 219 dead. House Wem had declared war over a long-standing grievance earlier that year. Throughout the period, the Second Crown of Reswoumark sent out four raids, all of which were beaten off, and suffered three raids, two of which carried off plunder. Five exiles returned to take service with the power, but four people were cast out. The power survived the period, but its authority had been repeatedly challenged and its military efforts consistently repelled.

House Wem entered the period as a victor, having just defeated the Sworn Men of Rucrag at Rucrag in year 49. The conflict with the Sworn Men ended in year 50 after two years of fighting left both sides exhausted, and peace was made. This resolution allowed House Wem to turn its attention outward. In year 51, the house declared war on the Second Crown of Reswoumark, citing a long-standing grievance. The war concluded quickly with a decisive victory for House Wem at Haelabarrow in year 51, where 219 men of the Second Crown died.

The period was also marked by internal violence within the Wougate Crown. In year 49, Kurnsa Bealldo had Threihoull Thild murdered at Rucrag. This pattern of assassination continued into year 50, when Kurnsa Bealldo had Skove Pull murdered at the same settlement. These killings occurred while the Wougate Crown’s raids on Wei Seam in year 49 and on Wougate in year 50 were both beaten off.

House Wem ended the period stronger than it began. It had secured peace with its regional rival, the Sworn Men of Rucrag, and had defeated the Second Crown of Reswoumark in battle. The house’s standing was defined by its military success against external powers, while the Wougate Crown was defined by internal purges and failed raids.

Kurnsa Bealldo took the seat of House Wem in 44 by election after Lea Dae was killed at Broldtemoor. In that same year, Mith Thres returned from exile to serve the house. The period ran for eight years, from 44 to 51. During this time, House Wem fought three battles, all of which were won. In 48, the house defeated the Sworn Men of Rucrag at Rucrag, killing 178. In 49, it defeated the Sworn Men of Rucrag again at Rucrag, killing 148. In 51, it defeated the Second Crown of Reswoumark at Haelabarrow, killing 219. The quarrel between House Wem and the Sworn Men of Rucrag persisted, resulting in two battles between them.

House Wem began two wars during the reign. The first was declared against the Sworn Men of Rucrag in 48 over a long-standing grievance. The house broke its alliance with them in 48 and made peace after two years in 50, with both sides exhausted. The second war was declared against the Second Crown of Reswoumark in 51 over a long-standing grievance, causing trade to break down. House Wem sent one raid, against Rucrag in 47, which got through but took nothing. It suffered five raids, all beaten off: by the Sworn Men of Rucrag at Broldtemoor in 44, by the Wougate Crown at Thu Pits in 45, by the Second Crown of Reswoumark at Wougate in 46, by the Wougate Crown at Wei Seam in 49, and by the Wougate Crown at Wougate in 50.

Kurnsa Bealldo ordered two killings against people of other powers: Threihoull Thild at Rucrag in 49 and Skove Pull at Rucrag in 50. Two of its own people were murdered from within by its own people. Two exiles returned to take service: Mith Thres in 44 and Drithne Draend in 47. Naerream Thrurei challenged Kurnsa Bealldo openly in 45 for the seat, lost, and Kurnsa Bealldo kept the seat. The Wougate Crown and the Second Crown of Reswoumark each publicly slighted House Wem in 48 and 49 respectively. The Sworn Men of Rucrag publicly slighted House Wem in 51. Kurnsa Bealldo was still holding the seat when the period ended in 51.

In year 51, House Wem declared war on the Second Crown of Reswoumark over a long-standing grievance, causing trade between the two powers to break down. Within the Crown, Voun Woldlom’s attempt on the life of Kurnsa Bealldo failed and was traced back to him. As a result of this attempted murder, Voun Woldlom was cast out of the Second Crown of Reswoumark.

House Wem defeated the Second Crown of Reswoumark at Haelabarrow, where 219 people died. Following the vacancy created by the casting out of Voun Woldlom, Greandoul Krean took the seat of the Second Crown of Reswoumark by right of birth.

The Wougate Crown declared war on the Reswoumark Crown in year 5 over Wei Seam. In that same year, the Wougate Crown and its allies defeated the Reswoumark Crown at Wei Seam, where 29 people died. The Wougate Crown took Wei Seam from the Reswoumark Crown as a result of the defeat.

In year 6, the Wougate Crown and its allies defeated the Reswoumark Crown at Reswoumark, with 198 dead. The Wougate Crown took Reswoumark from the Reswoumark Crown following this victory.

In year 7, the Wougate Crown and the Reswoumark Crown made peace after 2 years of fighting, following the collapse of the Reswoumark Crown.

House Wem declared war on the Wougate Crown in 22, citing a long-standing grievance. The Wougate Crown defeated House Wem at Thu Pits in 22, with 24 dead. The Wougate Crown defeated House Wem at Thu Pits again in 23, with 20 dead.

In 24, House Wem and its allies defeated the Wougate Crown at Thu Pits, with 16 dead. House Wem took Thu Pits from the Wougate Crown in 24. House Wem and its allies defeated the Wougate Crown at Wei Seam in 25, with 15 dead. House Wem took Wei Seam from the Wougate Crown in 25.

House Wem and the Wougate Crown made peace in 26 after 4 years, both sides exhausted.
